a. Improve baffling or increase chlorine dose
b. Reduce turbidity
c. Increase pH
d. Switch to ozone
Back: Answer: a. Improve baffling or increase chlorine dose

Front:
Chloramines require:
a. Higher CT than free chlorine
b. Lower CT
c. Same CT
d. No CT credit
Back: Answer: a. Higher CT than free chlorine

Front:
Disinfection profiling is required:
a. Before changing type or dose of disinfectant
b. During monthly testing
c. After main breaks
d. Only for systems >=10,000 people
Back: Answer: a. Before changing type or dose of disinfectant

Front:
If chlorine residual drops below 0.2 mg/L at entry point:
a. Treatment technique violation
b. No significance
c. Only aesthetic
d. Tier 3 notice
Back: Answer: a. Treatment technique violation

Front:
Title 22 CT tables are based on:
a. 99.9% Giardia inactivation
b. Virus only
c. 99% Giardia
d. 4-log virus
Back: Answer: a. 99.9% Giardia inactivation

Front:
Free chlorine CT tables assume:
a. Specific pH and temperature categories
b. pH irrelevant
c. All systems same CT
d. Turbidity = CT
Back: Answer: a. Specific pH and temperature categories

Front:
A plant operating at pH 9.2 should:
a. Use high CT or adjust pH downward
b. Reduce dose
c. Increase turbidity
d. Increase alkalinity
Back: Answer: a. Use high CT or adjust pH downward

Front:
CT is compromised if:
a. Tanks stratify due to low turnover
b. Turbidity decreases
c. pH decreases
d. Temperature increases
Back: Answer: a. Tanks stratify due to low turnover

Front:
Chlorine demand increases when:
a. Organic load increases
b. Alkalinity increases
c. Temperature decreases
d. pH decreases
Back: Answer: a. Organic load increases

Front:
Residual booster stations must:
a. Maintain detectable chlorine throughout system
b. Maintain 2.0 mg/L everywhere
c. Inject only at night
d. Use chloramines only
Back: Answer: a. Maintain detectable chlorine throughout system

Front:
A UV system offline requires:
a. Chlorine CT must fully meet requirements
b. No changes
c. Reduced monitoring
d. Raise pH
Back: Answer: a. Chlorine CT must fully meet requirements

Front:
CT credit cannot be given if:
a. Residual <=0.2 mg/L
b. Tank is baffled
c. pH <=7
d. Flow rate known
Back: Answer: a. Residual <=0.2 mg/L

Front:
A chlorine contact tank with dead zones results in:
a. Lower effective CT
b. Higher CT
c. No change
d. Higher residual
Back: Answer: a. Lower effective CT

Front:
A water system reduces flow but keeps dose same. CT:
a. Increases
b. Decreases
c. Unchanged
d. Must be recalculated but same
Back: Answer: a. Increases

Front:
A 4-log virus requirement applies to:
a. Surface water and GWUDI systems
b. Groundwater only
c. Recycled water only
d. Tanks only
Back: Answer: a. Surface water and GWUDI systems

Front:
Filter effluent exceeding 1.0 NTU:
a. Never-to-exceed violation
b. No issue
c. Annual report
d. pH adjustment only
Back: Answer: a. Never-to-exceed violation

Front:
Continuous turbidity monitoring is required for:
a. Each filter or combined filtered effluent
b. Raw water
c. Distribution system
d. Only plant effluent
Back: Answer: a. Each filter or combined filtered effluent

Front:
A combined filter effluent spike indicates:
a. Potential breakthrough; must investigate
b. Normal variation
c. No significance
d. Turbidity meter drift only
Back: Answer: a. Potential breakthrough; must investigate

Front:
A filter-to-waste requirement ensures:
a. Turbidity breakthrough is not sent to system
b. pH control
c. Corrosion control
d. Backflow prevention only
Back: Answer: a. Turbidity breakthrough is not sent to system

Front:
If a filter exceeds 1 NTU twice in 15 minutes:
a. Individual filter turbidity violation
b. No action
c. Backwash required only
d. Report annually
Back: Answer: a. Individual filter turbidity violation

Front:
SWTR requires:
a. 0.3 NTU 95% of time for conventional filtration
b. 0.1 NTU always
c. 2.0 NTU 95% of time
d. 1.0 NTU 95% of time
Back: Answer: a. 0.3 NTU 95% of time for conventional filtration

Front:
Poor coagulation increases:
a. Filter effluent turbidity
b. Residual
c. CT
d. TOC removal
Back: Answer: a. Filter effluent turbidity

Front:
If polymer feed stops:*a. Turbidity spikes likely
b. pH increases
c. DBPs decrease
d. CT increases
Back: Answer: (not marked)

Front:
Turbidity is a surrogate for: *a. Particle removal and pathogen
reduction
b. pH
c. Temperature
d. Alkalinity
Back: Answer: (not marked)

Front:
A plant must notify DDW if turbidity:
a. Exceeds 1.0 NTU at any time
b. Exceeds 0.1 NTU
c. Exceeds 2.0 NTU
d. Falls below 0.2 NTU
Back: Answer: a. Exceeds 1.0 NTU at any time

Front:
Filter profiling required when:
a. Significant turbidity changes occur
b. New operator hired
c. Filter media changes
d. Backwash schedule changes
Back: Answer: a. Significant turbidity changes occur

Front:
A filter with rapid turbidity rise post-backwash indicates:
a. Air binding or media damage
b. Low pH
c. High chlorine
d. Warm temperature
Back: Answer: a. Air binding or media damage

Front:
Individual filter monitoring identifies:
a. Breakthrough patterns
b. DBP formation
c. Corrosion
d. Nitrification
Back: Answer: a. Breakthrough patterns

Front:
Turbidity meter drift must be corrected: *a. Immediately;
turbidity is a critical parameter
b. Weekly
c. Monthly
d. Annually
Back: Answer: (not marked)

Front:
SWTR requires log removal credit based on:
a. Combined filter performance
b. Source water TOC
c. Flow rate only
d. TDS
Back: Answer: a. Combined filter performance

Front:
If multiple filters exceed turbidity standards:
a. TT violation likely
b. No action
c. Report annually
d. Switch to chloramines
Back: Answer: a. TT violation likely

Front:
Groundwater filtration is required if:
a. GWUDI is confirmed
b. TDS >=500 mg/L
c. Color >=15 CU
d. pH >=9
Back: Answer: a. GWUDI is confirmed

Front:
A filter failing turbidity standards repeatedly must:
a. Be removed from service and investigated
b. Continue operating
c. Report only monthly
d. Reduce dose only
Back: Answer: a. Be removed from service and investigated

Front:
Turbidity exceedances require:
a. Tier 2 notification
b. Tier 1
c. Tier 3
d. No notification
Back: Answer: a. Tier 2 notification

Front:
Source water turbidity >=5 NTU:
a. May require enhanced coagulation
b. Has no impact
c. Reduces CT
d. Indicates RTCR violation
Back: Answer: a. May require enhanced coagulation

Front:
A system with TC+ and EC+ (repeat) has:
a. An E. coli MCL violation
b. A TT violation
c. No violation
d. Tier 3 notice
Back: Answer: a. An E. coli MCL violation

Front:
TC+ routine but EC-:
a. Requires repeat sampling
b. Requires boil water notice
c. Is MCL violation
d. No action
Back: Answer: a. Requires repeat sampling

Front:
Repeat samples must be collected:
a. Within 24 hours
b. Within 48 hours
c. Within 72 hours
d. Within 1 week
Back: Answer: a. Within 24 hours

Front:
Level 1 assessment triggered when:
a. TC+ frequency exceeds threshold
b. Any EC+
c. Any TC+
d. Annual requirement
Back: Answer: a. TC+ frequency exceeds threshold

Front:
Level 2 assessment triggered when:
a. EC+ or repeat violations occur
b. Customer complaint
c. High pH
d. High THM
Back: Answer: a. EC+ or repeat violations occur

Front:
A missing bacteriological sample is:
a. Monitoring violation
b. MCL violation
c. TT violation
d. No violation
Back: Answer: a. Monitoring violation

Front:
Pressure <=5 psi requires:
a. Tier 1 notice
b. Tier 2 notice
c. Tier 3 notice
d. No notice
Back: Answer: a. Tier 1 notice

Front:
A main break with contamination potential requires:
a. Immediate sampling and corrective action
b. Annual report only
c. No sampling
d. Notify customers next CCR
Back: Answer: a. Immediate sampling and corrective action

Front:
Coliform-positive in distribution indicates:
a. Possible pathway of contamination
b. pH issue
c. CT issue
d. Turbidity issue
Back: Answer: a. Possible pathway of contamination

Front:
Cross-connection control program must:
a. Include annual testing of devices
b. Be voluntary
c. Be audited every 10 years
d. Only for recycled water
Back: Answer: a. Include annual testing of devices

Front:
Backflow device failure requires:
a. Immediate correction
b. No action
c. Annual only
d. Quarterly only
Back: Answer: a. Immediate correction

Front:
Storage tank contamination risk increases with:
a. Low turnover
b. High chlorine
c. Low turbidity
d. High pH
Back: Answer: a. Low turnover

Front:
Residual <=0.2 mg/L in distribution:
a. Potential TT violation
b. Acceptable
c. MCL violation
d. RTCR violation
Back: Answer: a. Potential TT violation

Front:
Stagnant zones in distribution result in:
a. DBP formation and nitrification
b. Lower turbidity
c. Higher pH
d. Lower TDS
Back: Answer: a. DBP formation and nitrification

Front:
Cross-connection inspections required:
a. Annually for high hazards
b. Every 10 years
c. Only during sanitary survey
d. After customer complaints
Back: Answer: a. Annually for high hazards

Front:
A hydrant sample shows 0 mg/L chlorine. Correct action:
a. Investigate and flush system
b. Ignore
c. Boost pH
d. Switch disinfectant
Back: Answer: a. Investigate and flush system

Front:
A storage tank exceeds 5 days retention:
a. Increased mixing required
b. Acceptable
c. Shut down tank
d. Raise pH
Back: Answer: a. Increased mixing required

Front:
Use of booster chlorination requires:
a. Permit and monitoring plan
b. No approval
c. Annual approval
d. Monthly approval
Back: Answer: a. Permit and monitoring plan

Front:
Pressure zone interconnection must:
a. Include backflow protection
b. Be unrestricted
c. Be unmonitored
d. Use chlorine only
Back: Answer: a. Include backflow protection

Front:
A system experiencing nitrification must:
a. Breakpoint chlorinate or flush
b. Reduce chlorine
c. Increase pH
d. Add polymer
Back: Answer: a. Breakpoint chlorinate or flush

Front:
Title 22 requires disinfected tertiary recycled water to meet:
a. Turbidity <=2 NTU daily average
b. Turbidity <=1 NTU
c. Turbidity <=10 NTU
d. Turbidity <=0.3 NTU
Back: Answer: a. Turbidity <=2 NTU daily average

Front:
Maximum allowable turbidity for recycled water:
a. 5 NTU never-to-exceed
b. 1 NTU
c. 10 NTU
d. 0.3 NTU
Back: Answer: a. 5 NTU never-to-exceed

Front:
Total coliform limit for disinfected tertiary is:
a. 2.2 MPN/100 mL 7-day median
b. 23 MPN/100 mL
c. 1 MPN/100 mL
d. 0 MPN/100 mL
Back: Answer: a. 2.2 MPN/100 mL 7-day median

Front:
Single TC result >=23 MPN/100mL requires: *a.
Immediate investigation and resampling
b. No action
c. Monthly reporting only
d. Only CCR notification
Back: Answer: (not marked)

Front:
Recycled water disinfection must provide:
a. 5-log virus removal/inactivation
b. 4-log virus
c. 2-log Giardia
d. 1-log Crypto
Back: Answer: a. 5-log virus removal/inactivation

Front:
Turbidity monitoring for recycled water must be:
a. Continuous
b. Monthly
c. Daily
d. Weekly
Back: Answer: a. Continuous

Front:
Recycled water treatment includes:
a. Coagulation, filtration, and disinfection
b. Filtration only
c. Aeration only
d. UV only
Back: Answer: a. Coagulation, filtration, and disinfection

Front:
Title 22 requires a Recycled Water User's Manual for:
a. All use sites
b. Sites >=10 acres
c. Agricultural only
d. Industrial only
Back: Answer: a. All use sites

Front:
Cross-connection testing for dual-plumbed systems must occur:
a. Every 4 years or as required
b. Every year
c. Every 10 years
d. Only at commissioning
Back: Answer: a. Every 4 years or as required

Front:
A recycled water system must:
a. Maintain purple pipe identification
b. Use blue pipe
c. Use green pipe
d. No color requirement
Back: Answer: a. Maintain purple pipe identification

Front:
For disinfected tertiary, filtration must meet:
a. 2 NTU daily average
b. 0.3 NTU
c. 5 NTU
d. 10 NTU
Back: Answer: a. 2 NTU daily average

Front:
Disinfection contact time for recycled water:
a. Must achieve 5-log virus removal
b. Must achieve 3-log bacteria
c. Is fixed at 30 minutes
d. Based only on pH
Back: Answer: a. Must achieve 5-log virus removal

Front:
Title 22 prohibits recycled water use for:
a. Direct human consumption
b. Irrigation
c. Industrial cooling
d. Dust control
Back: Answer: a. Direct human consumption

Front:
Recycled water impoundments must be:
a. Labeled and controlled to prevent access
b. Open to public
c. Mixed with potable water
d. Unmonitored
Back: Answer: a. Labeled and controlled to prevent access

Front:
Recycled water pipeline separation from potable water is typically:
a. >=10 feet horizontally
b. >=1 foot
c. No separation required
d. 50 feet minimum
Back: Answer: a. >=10 feet horizontally

Front:
A dual-plumbed building must:
a. Undergo initial and periodic cross-connection testing
b. Perform testing every 20 years
c. Be exempt from testing
d. Use any color pipe
Back: Answer: a. Undergo initial and periodic cross-connection testing

Front:
A recycled water use area must have:
a. Proper signage
b. No signage
c. Purple fencing only
d. Blue markings
Back: Answer: a. Proper signage

Front:
A recycled water system must notify DDW:
a. Prior to system modifications
b. Annually only
c. Only if requested
d. Only when customer complaints occur
Back: Answer: a. Prior to system modifications

Front:
High coliform in tertiary recycled water indicates:
a. Disinfection failure or filter breakthrough
b. pH problem
c. TDS issue
d. Corrosion
Back: Answer: a. Disinfection failure or filter breakthrough

Front:
Title 22 tertiary filtration must achieve:
a. 5-log Giardia removal through filtration + disinfection
b. 2-log virus
c. 1-log Crypto only
d. 3-log bacteria only
Back: Answer: a. 5-log Giardia removal through filtration + disinfection
